stemBlocks.value: Rewrite the quadratic expression 3x² − 12x + 7 by completing the square, in the form a(x + h)² + k.
Think first: The coefficient of x² is not 1, so factor the 3 out of the x-terms before you complete the square.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p101-q06 from workbook page 101.

solutionSteps.instruction: Factor 3 out of the terms containing x, leaving the constant outside.
Complete the square inside the bracket by halving the coefficient of x and squaring it.

contentBlocks.value: half of −4 is −2, and (−2)² = 4, so x² − 4x = (x − 2)² − 4

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the 3 back through the bracket.

strategyBlocks.value: Take 3 out of the first two terms, complete the square inside the bracket, then multiply back out and tidy the constant.

whyThisWorks.value: Completing the square rebuilds the quadratic around a single squared bracket, which is only possible when the x² coefficient inside is 1. Factoring the 3 out first creates that situation; multiplying it back afterwards scales the −4 into −12, which is why the constant changes. The identity is exact, so expanding 3(x − 2)² − 5 returns the original expression.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to multiply the subtracted square (−4) by the factor 3 when expanding the bracket back out.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to multiply the subtracted square (−4) by the factor 3 when expanding the bracket back out.

commonErrors.misconception: Factoring 3 out of the constant term as well, which is not needed and leads to fractions.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Factoring 3 out of the constant term as well, which is not needed and leads to fractions.

commonErrors.misconception: Halving −12 instead of −4 — the halving is done after the 3 is taken out.

examTip.value: After completing the square, expand your answer mentally to check it returns the original expression — it takes ten seconds and catches sign slips.
